prod_005:n1.prompt:
You are helping me set up product analytics by creating a new project in {{vendor}}, our chosen product-analytics platform. Please do the following:

1. If you don't already know it, ask me for: the {{vendor}} account/organization to use, the desired project name (e.g. matching my product or domain), and which environment this is for (production, staging, etc.).
2. Use your configured credentials to authenticate with {{vendor}}'s public API (or official CLI/MCP server if available).
3. Prepare the project creation request: project name, organization, and any relevant settings (timezone, data retention defaults) based on standard {{vendor}} project setup options. Check whether autocapture of clicks, pageviews, and form interactions can be enabled by default at project creation, and note the official SDKs available for web, mobile, and backend so we can wire up event tracking afterward.
4. Draft a clear summary showing: the exact project name and settings you intend to create, which organization it will belong to, and confirmation that no destructive or irreversible action will be taken without my approval.
5. Do NOT call the API to actually create the project yet. This step requires approval before changes are applied — stop for human sign-off once you have prepared the draft configuration and summary.
6. Report back with: the prepared project configuration, the exact API/CLI call you intend to run (in plain language, no raw credentials), and a short checklist of what will happen once I approve (project creation, autocapture status, SDK options for later steps).

Done looks like: a clear, reviewable plan for the {{vendor}} project creation is ready, nothing has been created yet, and you are waiting on my explicit go-ahead before executing the API/CLI call.

prod_005:n2.prompt:
You are helping me install PostHog’s product analytics SDK into our codebase so we get event tracking, funnels, and session recording. Before starting, ask me for: (1) the path or URL of the repository to work in, (2) the primary language/framework of the app (e.g., React, Next.js, Node backend, mobile), and (3) confirmation that a PostHog project already exists and that the project API key is available via my configured credentials or environment configuration — do not ask me to paste or reveal the key itself.

Once you have this, research the correct PostHog SDK for our stack (web JS snippet, npm package, or backend/server SDK as appropriate) and prepare the specific code changes: package install commands, initialization code referencing the API key through an environment variable or config reference (never hard-coded), placement of the snippet/init call in the right entry file, and any wrapper/provider setup needed for React or similar frameworks. Also prepare configuration for autocapture of events, session recording enablement, and any code hooks needed to later define funnels. Draft these as a proposed diff or pull request, not a direct commit to the main branch.

Summarize what you changed, why, and any manual verification steps needed (e.g., checking the PostHog dashboard for incoming events after deploy). Do not merge, deploy, or push these changes to production — present the diff/PR and configuration summary and then stop for human sign-off before applying anything further.

prod_005:n3.prompt:
You are helping me define key events for product analytics as part of setting up analytics with {{vendor}}. If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) my product's domain/app name, (2) which analytics vendor I've chosen (referred to below as {{vendor}}), (3) the core user actions that matter for my business (e.g., signup, purchase, feature activation), and (4) which platforms need tracking (web, mobile, backend).

Once you have this, do the following:
1. Draft a list of key events tailored to my product's core user journeys (e.g., signup, activation, conversion, retention actions), mapping each to the platform(s) it occurs on.
2. Note which of these events can be captured automatically via {{vendor}}'s autocapture of clicks, pageviews, and form interactions, so no custom tracking code is needed.
3. For events requiring custom tracking, prepare draft code snippets or API call descriptions using {{vendor}}'s official SDKs for the relevant languages/platforms (web, mobile, backend), describing the operations in words rather than inventing specific endpoints.
4. Check whether {{vendor}} exposes a documented public API for defining or managing events programmatically, and note how it could be used going forward.
5. Compile all of this into a clear checklist: event name, description, trigger source (auto vs custom), platform, and implementation snippet/description.

Do not apply any configuration changes, create events, or push code to {{vendor}} yet — this step requires my explicit approval before anything is implemented. Once your checklist and drafts are ready, present them to me and stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the full draft event list, which are auto-captured vs custom, the SDK/API approach for each platform, and confirmation that you are awaiting my approval before applying anything.

prod_005:n4.prompt:
You are helping me create product-analytics dashboards for my product using {{vendor}}, the analytics tool I've set up for event tracking, funnels, and session recording. If you don't already know it, ask me for: (1) my {{vendor}} workspace/project details, (2) the list of key metrics, saved insights, or events I want visualized (e.g., signups, activation funnel, retention, session recordings summary), and (3) any grouping/layout preferences for the dashboard(s).

Using your configured credentials, connect to {{vendor}}'s API or MCP server and prepare one or more dashboards composed of saved insights or reports covering the metrics I specify — for example, using a dashboard-creation operation (such as a 'Create Dashboard' call) that adds text cards and report/insight tiles for each metric. Draft the full dashboard structure: name, description, and the specific insights/cards it will contain, mapped to my key metrics.

Do not apply, submit, or publish any changes to my {{vendor}} account. Present the complete draft dashboard plan (names, layout, included insights, and data sources) to me in your report, along with the exact API/MCP calls or configuration you intend to run. Then stop for human sign-off — I will explicitly review and approve before you create anything live in {{vendor}}.

When reporting back, include: the proposed dashboard title(s), the list of insights/cards each will contain, how each maps to my stated key metrics, and any assumptions you made due to missing information. Flag anything ambiguous so I can clarify before approving.

prod_005:n5.prompt:
You are helping me set up product analytics funnels in {{vendor}}, our chosen product-analytics tool, so we can see where users drop off across key multi-step flows.

Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available, such as: my {{vendor}} workspace/project URL, the key user flows I want to analyze (e.g., signup, onboarding, checkout), the specific events or actions that make up each step of those flows, and any filters or breakdowns I want (e.g., by plan type, device, referral source, or user cohort).

Using your configured credentials, connect to {{vendor}}'s public API or dashboard and:
1. Review existing tracked events to confirm the events needed for each funnel already exist; note any gaps.
2. Draft 2-4 funnel insight definitions based on the flows I specify, each with ordered steps, relevant filters, and any breakdown dimensions I requested.
3. Include a sensible default time window and conversion window for each funnel unless I specify otherwise.
4. Prepare a clear summary showing each funnel's name, ordered steps, filters/breakdowns, and the reasoning for step selection (e.g., why a step marks a drop-off point).

Do not create or apply the funnels in {{vendor}} yet. This step requires a human to explicitly approve before changes are applied, so once your draft funnel definitions and summary are ready, stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the list of draft funnels (steps, filters, breakdowns, time windows), any event-tracking gaps you found that need to be fixed first, and any open questions about flow definitions or filters you need me to resolve before approval.

prod_005:n6.prompt:
You are helping me enable session recording in {{vendor}}, our product analytics tool, as part of setting up product analytics. Session recording will let me watch real user sessions and jump directly from funnel drop-offs or error events to the relevant replays.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available in our configured credentials or environment, such as: the {{vendor}} project/workspace name, our website domain, and confirmation of which environments (staging/production) should have recording enabled.

Then, using your configured credentials, prepare (but do not activate) the session recording setup in {{vendor}}:
1. Draft the recording configuration, including enabling session recording for the relevant project.
2. Confirm and document that sensitive input fields (passwords, payment fields, free-text inputs) are masked by default per {{vendor}}'s privacy settings, and note any additional fields we should mask given our product.
3. Identify and document how recordings can be linked to funnels and error/exception events so I can jump from a drop-off or error straight to the affected user's replay.
4. Prepare a written summary of the exact settings you would apply (recording toggle, masking rules, sampling rate if applicable, linkage to funnels/errors) so I can review before anything goes live.

Because enabling session recording requires my explicit approval before changes are applied, do not turn on recording or save/apply any configuration changes yourself. Present the full draft configuration and a checklist of what will change, then stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the draft configuration summary, the masking rules identified, how funnel/error-to-replay linkage will work, and a clear statement that you are awaiting my approval before applying anything.
